reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline (Jun/Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-05), driven by a defect in billing import validation rules that misclassifies/corrupts meter reads during import — producing incorrect bills across both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read types (E-01 shows ACTUAL reads are the majority, ~59%, of disputed bills, ruling out estimate-substitution as the dominant cause) — while tariff-rate changes are ruled out as a cause (E-02 shows zero logged tariff changes, corroborated by E-06).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-05), and the 1,240 disputed bills built on ESTIMATED reads (of 3,025 disputed bills total, E-01) trace to billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, unit_scaling=none, E-14) rejecting valid AMI reads from firmware-v4.2 meters as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1,184 such reads, E-12) because v4.2 reports consumption in '0.1 m3' units that appear ~10x inflated against m3-based history (E-13), forcing those accounts onto disputed estimated bills. This confirmed BV-17/firmware-unit mechanism explains the ESTIMATED-read dispute population but does not yet account for the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills that form the stated majority (59%, E-01).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
